label: Copy-phase input is one of g/p/t/k/r/j
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never on original tokens or the <DEL> step, and never at recall_idx 0. Within the copy phase it is selective for the fed-back input token: g and p (~31% rate) > t, k (~20-23%) > r, j (~15-17%), with y weakly and other tokens rarely. The predicate (copy phase AND input in {g,p,t,k,r,j}) captures ~92% of activation mass and 85% of active steps but only ~50% precision: the same tokens are often silent, especially as the first copy input (recall_idx 1) and later in long copies. Activation is strongest early in the copy (recall_idx 2-3, t ~10-12) and in runs of consecutive preferred tokens (e.g. g p k t right after <DEL>); restricting to recall_idx >= 2 raises precision to 0.55 but loses mass. Does not fire in the original phase.
